comments.note: The dark theme section at the bottom of styles.css is growing incrementally (badge overrides, banner overrides, form overrides, now run log overrides). As the file grows, consider co-locating dark-theme rules directly beneath their light-theme counterparts (or use CSS layers) to improve maintainability. This is not urgent but will pay off as more features are added.

.run-progress-bar uses var(--color-ready) as the fill color, consistent with .progress-bar-fill in the existing progress bar. This is fine semantically for now but worth noting: if the run log viewer needs a different fill color in future, a dedicated --color-run-progress token would prevent unintended color coupling.

summary: Reviewed styles.css run log viewer section (lines 1697-1801) — CSS-only addition appended at end of file.
Namespace check: all 17 new selectors use the .run-* prefix — confirmed zero conflicts with any existing selector in the file.

AC-1 (.run-event--info/warning/error distinct left-border colors): .run-event base sets border-left: 4px solid var(--color-border) as a neutral fallback; each modifier overrides border-left-color with --color-ready (blue), --color-in-progress (amber), --color-blocked (red) respectively. Clean BEM pattern, well-implemented.

AC-2 (.run-progress-bar width via inline style only): confirmed — .run-progress-bar declares height: 100%, background, border-radius, transition but NO width rule. The JSDoc comment in the CSS reinforces this contract. Correct.

AC-3 (no CSS errors, no selector conflicts): all referenced custom properties (--color-surface, --color-border, --radius, --radius-pill, --color-ready, --color-in-progress, --color-blocked, --color-complete, --color-text-muted, --color-bg) exist in the :root block. No orphaned variables.

AC-4 (dark theme via --color-* variables): --color-ready, --color-in-progress, --color-blocked already have dark-mode values in the [data-theme='dark'] :root block. The three explicit [data-theme='dark'] .run-event--* rules re-declare the same variables — technically redundant but serve as explicit documentation anchors. The stage badge dark overrides (lines 1785-1800) use explicit hex values appropriate for dark backgrounds, consistent with other badge dark overrides in the file.
AC-5 (no regression): .run-* namespace is entirely new; no existing selector is modified or overridden.
transition: width 0.2s ease on .run-progress-bar will work correctly when JS updates the inline width style — this is the correct pattern for animated progress bars.
All 5 acceptance criteria confirmed met.

comments.note: Lines 1781-1783: [data-theme='dark'] .run-event--info/warning/error re-declare the same --color-* variable values as light mode. Because CSS custom properties cascade through the [data-theme='dark'] :root block, these rules resolve correctly but are redundant. They add no functional value; their only benefit is as documentation anchors. No change required — logging for awareness.

.run-progress-bar background: var(--color-ready) reuses the status-ready blue for progress fill. This is consistent with .progress-bar-fill elsewhere in the file, but creates implicit color coupling: any future restyling of --color-ready for status badges will also affect the progress bar fill. A dedicated --color-progress-fill token would decouple these concerns. Low priority.

styles.css [data-theme='dark'] block continues to grow as an append-only section at the bottom of the file. This is the second or third WP to note this pattern. As the file grows, dark-theme rules separated from their light counterparts become harder to maintain. Consider co-locating per-component or creating a separate dark-theme partial if a build step is introduced.
